traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified.
Mapping to key requirements: - **REQ-RULE-NAME / Rule Naming**: `src/index.ts` wires `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` as the primary rule name and marks `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias with `meta.deprecated = true` and `meta.replacedBy = ["prefer-supports-annotation"]`. The dedicated test file runs the same rule implementation under both names, confirming aliasing. - **REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING**: `processComment` in `src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts` reports `messageId: "preferImplements"` whenever legacy `@story` + `@req` are detected. The tests include cases with single-story legacy blocks and confirm the warning for both rule keys. - **REQ-AUTO-FIX / REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX / REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT / REQ-VALID-OUTPUT**: The auto-fix path (`collectStoryAndReqMetadata`, `buildImplementsAutoFix`, `applyImplementsReplacement`) only produces a fix when there is exactly one `@story` line, at least one simple `@req` line, and no extra tokens, ensuring safe single-story conversion. It replaces the original `@story` line with a `@supports ` line, leaving other lines (such as description, @param, @returns) untouched, preserving order and formatting. Tests verify conversion for single `@req` and multiple `@req` lines, and verify that more complex lines (extra description content in `@story` or `@req`) do NOT auto-fix but still warn. - **REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT**: `analyzeComment` collects distinct story paths; `hasMultipleStories` with threshold >1 triggers `messageId: "multiStoryDetected"`. Mixed usage with existing `@supports` triggers `cannotAutoFix` with an explanatory `reason`. Tests cover both the mixed and multiple-story cases. - **REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY**: Rule `meta.docs.recommended` is false and the rule is absent from both `recommended` and `strict` presets (verified by tests), so it is disabled by default. The configuration test demonstrates enabling both primary and alias names with `"warn"` or `"error"`, confirming support for the required severities. - **REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION / Both Formats Valid**: The rule only inspects comments and adds diagnostics; it does not run when configured "off" and never enforces changes by itself. Valid test cases verify that comments containing only `@story`, only `@req`, only `@supports`, or various @supports-without-req/@story combinations are ignored by this rule even when enabled. Combined with existing validation rules (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, valid-annotation-format, etc., which all have passing tests), this satisfies the requirement that `@story`/`@req` remain valid regardless of this recommendation rule. - **REQ-VALID-OUTPUT / Integration with @supports validation**: The auto-fix generates `@supports` lines in the format already validated by `valid-annotation-format` and related rules (`@supports storyPath REQ-IDs`). Other tests confirm parsing and validation of this format, so the generated lines are accepted by the existing `@supports` infrastructure. - **Documentation**: `user-docs/migration-guide.md` contains an explicit section on the optional `prefer-supports-annotation` rule, explaining behavior, auto-fix semantics, ignored cases, configuration examples, and the continued support of legacy annotations. `README.md` lists the rule, notes that it is disabled by default, and describes the deprecated alias. This matches the story’s documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the concrete code, targeted tests referencing this story, successful focused test run, and aligned documentation, the story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS is fully implemented.
